app.name: HeatSense
app.tagline: From heat maps to heat action.
app.subheading: Heat-risk mapping and action-planning platform for municipal officers in Hyderabad, India.
app.sampleData: Sample data shown for demonstration and planning simulation.

hero.headline: See where heat is most dangerous. Act where it matters most.
hero.subheading: Cities lack street-level data on heat risks. HeatSense transforms satellite thermal telemetry and census vulnerability into prioritized municipal cooling interventions and life-saving alerts.

stats.stat1Desc: People in India each experienced nearly 20 heatwave days in 2024, about 6.5 of them directly linked to climate change.
stats.stat1Source: Source: Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change 2025
stats.stat2Desc: Heat exposure caused 247 billion potential labour hours lost in India in 2024 — equivalent to about 420 hours per person.
stats.stat2Source: Source: Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change 2025
stats.stat3Desc: Potential income loss of ~$194B across India, with agriculture representing 66% and construction 20% of acute losses.
stats.stat3Source: Source: Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change 2025

whoFaces.title: Who Faces This Problem?
whoFaces.subtitle: Urban heat does not fall equally. HeatSense identifies and shields Hyderabad's most vulnerable populations.
whoFaces.group1Desc: Living in informal or dense settlements with uninsulated tin or concrete roofs, low ventilation and minimal tree canopy.
whoFaces.group2Desc: Delivery riders, street vendors, sanitation crews and construction laborers exposed to 7+ hours of intense midday radiation.
whoFaces.group3Desc: Physiologically vulnerable individuals unable to thermoregulate efficiently during extreme ambient temperature spikes.
whoFaces.group4Desc: Municipal teams managing scarce budgets who lack ward-level diagnostic heat maps to guide tree planting and shade shelters.
whoFaces.group5Desc: Grid operators facing sudden transformer overloads and feeder trips driven by surging AC cooling demand during peak hours.

howWorks.title: How HeatSense Works
howWorks.subtitle: Closing the loop from satellite data to on-ground municipal action in four synchronized stages.
howWorks.step1Desc: Ingest high-resolution satellite thermal imagery (Landsat & Sentinel-2) to measure true Land Surface Temperature across all 40 Hyderabad wards.
howWorks.step2Desc: Layer street-level socio-demographic vulnerability: elderly, young children, non-AC households, and outdoor labor density.
howWorks.step3Desc: Run automated optimization algorithms that suggest high-impact interventions: cool roofs, urban canopies, misting lines and drinking kiosks.
howWorks.step4Desc: Broadcast hyperlocal multilingual heatwave alerts via SMS & WhatsApp directly to outdoor gig workers and at-risk residents.

features.title: Built for Decision Makers
features.subtitle: Everything city leaders need to anticipate heat emergencies and invest resilience capital efficiently.
features.feat1Desc: A composite 0-100 metric balancing surface heat, canopy deficit, built density and population vulnerability.
features.feat2Desc: Greedy optimization engine that generates prioritized intervention plans tailored to municipal budget constraints.
features.feat3Desc: Test cooling scenarios: adjust tree canopy, cool roofs, or shade canopies to predict temperature drops and power savings.
features.feat4Desc: Draft, preview and dispatch targeted WhatsApp & SMS safety bulletins in English, Telugu and Hindi.
features.feat5Desc: Track peak AC-driven power spikes, overload risks, and target demand-response nudges.
features.feat6Desc: Export print-ready PDF briefs and CSV datasets formatted for council reviews and field operations.

about.title: Methodology, Data Sources & Validation
about.subtitle: How HeatSense turns satellite science into accountable municipal governance.
about.formulaDesc: Heat-Risk Score = wTemp × Norm(Temp) + wTree × (1 - Norm(Tree)) + wBuilt × Norm(Built) + wVuln × VulnIndex

safety.tip1: Drink 3-4 liters of water throughout the day, even if you do not feel thirsty.
safety.tip2: Avoid direct outdoor sun exposure between 11:30 AM and 3:30 PM.
safety.tip3: Wear lightweight, loose-fitting, light-colored cotton clothes and wide-brimmed hats.
safety.tip4: Never leave children, infants or pets in parked vehicles even with windows cracked.
safety.tip5: Know heat stroke danger signs: dizziness, nausea, rapid pulse, lack of sweat. Call 108 immediately.
